transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Giles Snyder.
Defense Secretary Pete Hexeth could face a House vote on impeachment later this week.
Kentucky Republican Congressman Thomas Massey filed an impeachment resolution Monday
as a House open backup following the midterm elections.
Here's NPR's Sam Greenglass.
Massey says he doesn't know if there are enough votes to impeach,
but he really only needs a couple of Republicans, which is totally possible.
Now, if Hexeth is impeached in the House, it's up to the Senate to hold a trial,
and over there it would take 67 senators to convict, which is a very high bar.
Hexeth says he's not worried, and President Trump told reporters at the White House
that he will stand by Hexeth.
He also called Congressman Massey a stone-cold loser.
After meeting at the White House Monday with Qatar's Prime Minister,
President Trump said he plans to hold off on new military strikes against Iran for the time being.
Trump said he made the decision to keep the status quo at the best of countries in the region,
saying they prefer the U.S. not launch new attacks,
but he said he plans to keep up a naval blockade in the Strait of Hormuz for now.
The Supreme Court is allowing the federal government to move forward
with construction of hundreds of miles of border barriers in West Texas as the lawsuit moves forward.
Carlos Morales reports.
The justices said, in part, because the law allows the federal government to waive environmental protections,
there's a "clear preference" for expeditious border construction
over the harms laid out in the lawsuit that had halted construction in Texas' Big Bend region.
Lakin Jordan is with the Center for Biological Diversity, one of the groups that brought the suit.
This decision green lights the contractors and allows the bulldozers to come roaring back into the region.
The Trump administration's plans for the Big Bend stirred up bipartisan backlash
with people uniting in their belief that security infrastructure isn't needed in the region.
For NPR News, I'm Carlos Morales in Marfa, Texas.
NVIDIA is investigating its CEO Jensen Wang after news outlets reported he had an affair with a possible Chinese spy.
But NVIDIA's drama has been overshadowed by traders' shifting feelings about what the midterm elections mean for tech stocks.
They've swung up and down since election night, most recently swinging up, NVIDIA not included.
Lower oil prices also calm investors.
Crude oil futures are down about 4.5% and selling at about $86 a barrel.
That follows the Trump administration signaling restraint in terms of future strikes against Iran.
Stephen Misaha, NPR News.
With oil prices easing Asian stocks following Wall Street higher,
South Korean shares leading the way up more than 3.5%.
This is NPR News.
Another top Justice Department official is stepping down.
Attorney General Todd Blanche announced the resignation of civil division leader Brett Shumate in a Monday post on social media.
Shumate is at least the third senior Justice Department official to resign since Democrats won control of Congress last week.
Lindsey Clancy has lost her bid to have the murder charges against her dismissed.
A judge of Massachusetts Monday denied a motion to dismiss, potentially clearing the way for a retrial in the deaths of her three young children.
In September, the judge declared a mistrial after the jury reported a holdout was preventing a unanimous verdict.
New research points to the role of circadian rhythms in depression.
A study from a team at the University of Sydney suggests that as many as one in four people with the diagnosis
could have a distinct type of depression rooted in problems with their circadian rhythms.
Here's NPR's Will Stone.
The study used a database of about 10,000 adults in Australia with depression.
The researchers came up with different criteria.
They looked at sleep schedule, whether people were a night owl, their level of tiredness in the morning and more.
Based on that, they found just under 25 percent of adults fit this profile for circadian depression.
A key finding was that they tended to have less success with SSRIs, the most commonly prescribed class of antidepressants.
The study was published in the British Journal of Psychiatry.
The authors emphasized the study is a proof of concept and needs to be replicated in other populations,
but it could eventually help steer patients to treatments that are more likely to work.
Will Stone, NPR News.
And I'm Giles Snyder. This is NPR News.
